title: Episode 194: The One Thing Every Programmer Should Know with Kevlin Henney

sentences.en: My 1890s French carriage clock.
sentences.zh: 我那台1890年代的法国座钟。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 194, recorded on July 11th, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听ADSP播客，第194期，录制于2024年7月11日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we finish our five-part conversation with Kevlin Henney and chat about the one thing every programmer should know.
sentences.zh: 我是Connor，今天和我的联合主持人Bryce一起，我们将结束与Kevlin Henney的五部分系列访谈，聊聊每个程序员都应该知道的一件事。

sentences.en: One final and important question for, I suppose, both of you could answer.
sentences.zh: 我想，最后有一个重要的问题，你们两位或许都能回答。

sentences.en: And it's a very Bryce question, which is, you, Kevlin, have written a book,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常“Bryce式”的问题，那就是，Kevlin，你写过一本书，

sentences.en: 97 Things Every Programmer Should Know.
sentences.zh: 《每个程序员都应该知道的97件事》。

sentences.en: But as listeners of this podcast will know, I, Bryce, don't have time for such things.
sentences.zh: 但正如本播客的听众所知，我，Bryce，没时间看这些东西。

sentences.en: So can you tell me what is the one thing that every programmer should know?
sentences.zh: 所以你能告诉我，每个程序员都应该知道的那一件事是什么吗？

sentences.en: Ah, right.
sentences.zh: 啊，好吧。

sentences.en: So just a minor correction.
sentences.zh: 先做一个小小的更正。

sentences.en: I didn't write it.
sentences.zh: 那本书不是我写的。

sentences.en: I edited it.
sentences.zh: 是我编辑的。

sentences.en: I ran the project.
sentences.zh: 我负责这个项目。

sentences.en: I kind of got everything.
sentences.zh: 我算是把所有东西整合在了一起。

sentences.en: I contributed a few items that I wrote, but therefore it is a crowdsourced and open-source book.
sentences.zh: 我贡献了其中几篇我写的文章，但它本质上是一本众包和开源的书。

sentences.en: So, yes, it actually is under Creative Commons license.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它实际上是在知识共享许可协议（Creative Commons）下发布的。

sentences.en: That was intentional on my part.
sentences.zh: 这是我刻意为之的。

sentences.en: So you can actually find a few versions kicking around online every now and then I get.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上可以在网上找到几个版本，时不时我就会收到……

sentences.en: Yeah, you're not allowed to have the PDF of the book, but the original entries were originally available on a wiki.
sentences.zh: 是的，你没被允许拥有那本书的PDF，但原始条目最初是在一个Wiki上发布的。

sentences.en: And so I've had people have scraped this and put this into Gitbooks and GitHub in various places.
sentences.zh: 所以有人抓取了这些内容，并把它们放到了Gitbooks和GitHub的各个地方。

sentences.en: So you don't have to buy the book.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要买这本书。

sentences.en: You can find the items online if you wish.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，可以在网上找到这些条目。

sentences.en: And that's perfectly okay.
sentences.zh: 这完全没问题。

sentences.en: The reason I'm saying it's perfectly okay is because occasionally I get an email from somebody saying, hey, guess what?
sentences.zh: 我之所以说完全没问题，是因为偶尔会有人给我发邮件说，嘿，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: Did you know somebody's ripped off your book?
sentences.zh: 你知道有人盗用了你的书吗？

sentences.en: And no, it's intentional.
sentences.zh: 不，这是故意的。

sentences.en: Creative Commons license, that's absolutely fine.
sentences.zh: 知识共享许可协议，这完全没问题。

sentences.en: They can't rip off the PDF.
sentences.zh: 他们不能盗用PDF。

sentences.en: That's kind of differently copyrighted.
sentences.zh: 那是有不同版权保护的。

sentences.en: But the individual items, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但对于单个条目，绝对没问题。

sentences.en: They're under Creative Commons.
sentences.zh: 它们都在知识共享协议下。

sentences.en: Now, why am I telling you all of this?
sentences.zh: 现在，我为什么要告诉你们这些呢？

sentences.en: Well, that so that we don't inspire more emails to me that are necessary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是为了让我不再收到那些不必要的邮件。

sentences.en: But also to allow people to do this if they don't want to part dollars.
sentences.zh: 同时也是为了让那些不想花钱的人也能看到这些内容。

sentences.en: But more importantly, there are lots of contributors to that book.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，那本书有很多贡献者。

sentences.en: So I've got an opt-out of this question that you've just asked because I'm not going to pick favourites.
sentences.zh: 所以我对你刚才问的这个问题有“豁免权”，因为我不会偏袒任何一个人。

sentences.en: There are 73 contributors to that book.
sentences.zh: 那本书有73位贡献者。

sentences.en: I'm not going to pick one because that's unfair on the other 72.
sentences.zh: 我不会选出其中一个，因为这对其他72个人不公平。

sentences.en: So I've got a get-out clause here that Colin doesn't have.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个Connor没有的“脱身条款”。

sentences.en: Ah, yes.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的。

sentences.en: So Connor, what is the one thing that every programmer should know?
sentences.zh: 那么Connor，每个程序员都应该知道的那一件事是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I just went and, you know, found the get thing because I'm trying to find the one of the five because I'm pretty sure that one of the things in the 97 things is it quotes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我刚才去查了一下，你知道，找到了那个东西，因为我想找出那五件事中的一件，我非常确定《97件事》里的其中一件事引用了它。

sentences.en: I'm not going to remember the name of the book because the original quote comes from another book.
sentences.zh: 我记不住书名了，因为原始引文来自另一本书。

sentences.en: And I've mentioned this in talks before.
sentences.zh: 我以前在演讲中提到过这一点。

sentences.en: But basically, like, I think potentially it's learn foreign languages.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，我觉得可能是“学习外语”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I've gone to that.
sentences.zh: 但我刚才去看了。

sentences.en: There's learn foreign languages.
sentences.zh: 确实有“学习外语”这一条。

sentences.en: That one, if I remember correctly, is Klaus Markfart.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，那是Klaus Markfart写的。

sentences.en: There is another one, no more than one language well, if I remember correctly.
sentences.zh: 还有另一条，如果我没记错的话，是“精通不超过一门语言”。

sentences.en: No more than two, no well more than two programming languages.
sentences.zh: “精通不超过两门，嗯，不超过两门编程语言”。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was from Russell Winder.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是Russell Winder写的。

sentences.en: So, but wait, wait, Kevlin.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，Kevlin。

sentences.en: So I may have to revoke you out.
sentences.zh: 我可能得撤销你的豁免权了。

sentences.en: And the reason is these things are numbered, which means that somebody had to pick which one was going to be number one.
sentences.zh: 原因在于这些条目是有编号的，这意味着有人必须选出哪一个是第一名。

sentences.en: Ah, right.
sentences.zh: 啊，好吧。

sentences.en: They are, strictly speaking, in the original book, they are not numbered.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，在原书中，它们是没有编号的。

sentences.en: They are numbered in the electronic copies.
sentences.zh: 它们是在电子版中才被编号的。

sentences.en: Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: But if you look at the titles, you will understand how I ordered it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看标题，你就会明白我是如何排序的。

sentences.en: Is it alphabetical?
sentences.zh: 是按字母顺序吗？

sentences.en: It is alphabetical.
sentences.zh: 是的，是按字母顺序。

sentences.en: Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: Because I thought, I can't play favorites.
sentences.zh: 因为我想，我不能偏袒任何人。

sentences.en: But also, if you try and group things by topic.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你试图按主题对它们进行分组。

sentences.en: It's very hard to group things.
sentences.zh: 很难把它们归类。

sentences.en: It's very, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实非常难。

sentences.en: You often find one, you find a piece and it's actually under two good, you can file it under equally well under two different.
sentences.zh: 你经常会发现一篇文章，它其实属于两个……你可以把它同样好地归入两个不同的类别。

sentences.en: Categorizing stuff.
sentences.zh: 分类这事儿。

sentences.en: Like, as somebody who's in the role of being a software architect, like, taking ideas and concepts and, like, categorizing them is, like, one of the, it's, like, a big part of the
sentences.zh: 作为一名软件架构师，获取想法和概念，并将它们分类，是工作中的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: job.
sentences.zh: 工作。

sentences.en: And it's also one of the hardest things.
sentences.zh: 这也是最难的事情之一。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I chose, so it's interesting how other 97 Things books in that series have chosen to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我选择……有趣的是，该系列中其他《97件事》的书是如何选择排序的。

sentences.en: The original, the original 97 Things Every Software Architect Should Know had the most arbitrary order.
sentences.zh: 最初的《每个软件架构师都应该知道的97件事》的排序最随意。

sentences.en: So I was originally part of the group.
sentences.zh: 我当时也是该小组的一员。

sentences.en: I could kind of make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 我还能勉强理解它。

sentences.en: But when it was published, it was the order in which they were submitted.
sentences.zh: 但当它出版时，它是按照提交的顺序排列的。

sentences.en: Now, that is utterly meaningless to anybody reading the book.
sentences.zh: 这对任何读这本书的人来说都毫无意义。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't know what order they were submitted.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你根本不知道它们是按什么顺序提交的。

sentences.en: Why is that useful?
sentences.zh: 那有什么用呢？

sentences.en: So it meant that sometimes, you know, that you'd end up with topics that you could, you'd say, well, why is this person has submitted two items?
sentences.zh: 这意味着有时，你知道，你会发现一些主题，你会说，为什么这个人提交了两篇？

sentences.en: Why are they next to each other?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们挨在一起？

sentences.en: And then this other person who submitted two items, their items are like 50 pages apart.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个人也提交了两篇，但他们的文章却隔了50页。

sentences.en: Well, that's literally the timeline.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那实际上就是时间线。

sentences.en: Well, I guess one could argue that the people who had their shit the most together probably submitted early.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有人可能会说，那些准备得最充分的人可能提交得比较早。

sentences.en: And so at the very least, those were the people who, or those were the ones that had the most urgency and the people who were best at like getting it done on a deadline.
sentences.zh: 所以至少，这些人是那些最有紧迫感，或者最擅长在截止日期前完成任务的人。

sentences.en: So that's not a terrible mechanism.
sentences.zh: 所以这也不是一个糟糕的机制。

sentences.en: That's a very positive way of framing it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常积极的解读方式。

sentences.en: On the other hand, maybe they just got something done and they didn't have, they didn't let something gestate and mature over time.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，也许他们只是完成了任务，而没有让想法经过沉淀和成熟。

sentences.en: So maybe the ones at the back of the book are better because people were more deliberate about them and they'd let the ideas sit with them for longer.
sentences.zh: 所以也许书后面的文章更好，因为人们对它们更深思熟虑，让想法在脑海中停留了更长时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, both of these lines of argument work.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这两种论点都成立。

sentences.en: I do like, I do like the first one, which is Act with Prudence.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢第一条，也就是“审慎行事”（Act with Prudence）。

sentences.en: Yeah, by Seth Rose.
sentences.zh: 是的，Seth Rose写的。

sentences.en: I think that's a, that's a, that's a good one, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一篇很好的文章。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's kind of interesting is, is that, that alphabetically that one, you know, that's obviously first, but also actually it's quite a good opening to the book.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，按字母顺序排列，那篇显然排在第一位，但实际上它也是这本书很好的开篇。

sentences.en: You know, I was, I was delighted by the coincidence because obviously reverse order was also an option,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我对这个巧合感到很高兴，因为显然倒序也是一种选择，

sentences.en: but I decided up front, there's no rational way of organizing 97 things when you don't know what 97 things you're going to get.
sentences.zh: 但我一开始就决定了，当你不知道会收到哪97件事时，没有理性的方式来组织它们。

sentences.en: I tried putting categories on them, but I already knew it was a, it's a library problem in the sense of like, there's no natural structure here.
sentences.zh: 我试过给它们分类，但我已经知道这是一个“图书馆问题”，意思是这里没有自然的结构。

sentences.en: If I'm creating a book from scratch and I solicit individual items explicitly, I can say, we want this, this, this, this, this is my vision for the book.
sentences.zh: 如果我是从零开始创作一本书，并明确征集各个条目，我可以要求：我们想要这个、这个、这个，这是我对这本书的愿景。

sentences.en: But this is very much an emergent architecture where I got, you know, I got nearly 200 submissions.
sentences.zh: 但这是一次非常“涌现式”的架构，我收到了近200份投稿。

sentences.en: It was around 100, it was around towards 170.
sentences.zh: 大约是100份，接近170份左右。

sentences.en: And what you've got to do is kind of say, here's what I've got.
sentences.zh: 你必须要做的是说，这就是我手头有的东西。

sentences.en: What can I make with it?
sentences.zh: 我能用它们做些什么？

sentences.en: You know, it's, it's, you know, it's, it's go to the fridge and I don't know what happened with your fridge there, Bryce, but you know, I don't know what the narrative is with the
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像是去冰箱找吃的，我不知道你的冰箱发生了什么，Bryce，但我不知道关于冰箱的叙述是什么，

sentences.en: fridge, but it's go to your fridge and I go to the fridge.
sentences.zh: 但就是去你的冰箱，我去冰箱找吃的。

sentences.en: I'm hungry.
sentences.zh: 我饿了。

sentences.en: Go to the fridge.
sentences.zh: 去冰箱。

sentences.en: I need to make a meal.
sentences.zh: 我需要做顿饭。

sentences.en: What have I got?
sentences.zh: 我有什么食材？

sentences.en: So you, in other words, something emerges from that without necessarily saying I am planning to make this meal.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，事情就是这样自然而然地产生的，而不必预先计划好我要做这顿饭。

sentences.en: So I chose alphabetical and I did that in the other 97 Things book as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我选择了按字母顺序，我在另一本《97件事》书中也是这么做的。

sentences.en: It's that alphabetical is the only rational way to allow people to find things.
sentences.zh: 按字母顺序是让人们找到内容的唯一理性方式。

sentences.en: All other approaches are arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 所有其他方法都是随意的。

sentences.en: Let me tell you that the other arbitrary approach that was used, one of the other arbitrary approaches that was used was for 97 Things Every Project Manager Should Know.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你，另一种被使用的随意方法，其中一种被用于《每个项目经理都应该知道的97件事》的方法。

sentences.en: That was interesting because I was looking at it going like, I can't see any sense to the ordering of these.
sentences.zh: 那很有趣，因为我看着它觉得，我看不出这些排序有什么逻辑。

sentences.en: The editor of that book decided that the ordering of the book should alternate U.S.
sentences.zh: 那本书的编辑决定书的排序应该交替使用美国贡献者和非美国贡献者。

sentences.en: contributors from non-U.S.
sentences.zh: 交替使用。

sentences.en: contributors or U.S.-based contributors from non-U.S.-based contributors.
sentences.zh: 或者说美国本土贡献者和非美国本土贡献者。

sentences.en: Honestly, that's almost as good as random number generation.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这几乎和随机数生成一样好。

sentences.en: I think that's a good approach because it accounts for some of the bias of a lot of tech is very U.S.-centric and based in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种很好的方法，因为它考虑到了很多科技行业非常以美国为中心、总部设在美国的偏见。

sentences.en: But the point is that if half your items are U.S.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，如果你的条目有一半是美国的，一半不是，实际上并没有一个正确的顺序。

sentences.en: and half of them are not, there isn't actually, I would say, there isn't a white order.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，有道理。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay, fair point.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果我读第一篇是美国作者，第二篇是非美国作者，第三篇……那不是再次找到该条目的有用标准。

sentences.en: Yeah, if I read the first one, U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: author, second one, non-U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道。

sentences.en: author, third, that's not a useful criteria for finding that item again.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以关于代表性的问题确实是一个重要的问题，也是我绝对处理过的问题。

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 所以我试着在第一本书中处理它，取得了一定的成功，但没有我们在第二本书中做得那么好。

sentences.en: I would agree.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是说，这就是我们排序条目的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the question of representation is certainly an important one and is definitely something I dealt with.
sentences.zh: 这真的没什么用。

sentences.en: So I tried dealing with it with moderate success on the first book, but not as much as we managed on the second one.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个作者是不是美国的。

sentences.en: But it's the idea of like, this is how we're going to order the iteMs.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's just like, that's not useful.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我看不出来。

sentences.en: I don't know if this author is U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这对我也没帮助。

sentences.en: or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我构建了它，并且我特意在书的后面放了一个反向索引。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能记得，哦，我记得那件事是某某人写的，你知道，是这个人写的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I can't tell.
sentences.zh: 让我看看，我能记住名字，但记不住标题。

sentences.en: You know, that's not helpful to me.
sentences.zh: 所以我按名字的字母顺序排列了。

sentences.en: I can't, so I structured it, and I intentionally put in a reverse lookup as well at the back of the book.
sentences.zh: 有匿名的或者用笔名的吗？

sentences.en: So you might remember, oh, I remember the thing was written by somebody, by so-and-so, you know, by this person.
sentences.zh: 有一个是用笔名的。

sentences.en: Let me, I can remember the name, but I can't remember the title.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I did it alphabetical by name.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Are any anonymous or under pseudonyms?
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: There's one that is a pseudonym.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And how did you pick, why 97?
sentences.zh: 那你是怎么选的，为什么是97？

sentences.en: This is a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: It wasn't me that originally picked it.
sentences.zh: 最初并不是我选的。

sentences.en: As I mentioned, it emerged, it got created out of a separate discussion, a separate liSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，它是自然产生的，是在一次单独的讨论、一份单独的列表中创建出来的。

sentences.en: It's a list that Bruce Eccle maintains.
sentences.zh: 那是一份由布鲁斯·埃克尔（Bruce Eckel）维护的列表。

sentences.en: So some listeners may be faintly aware of Bruce Eccle.
sentences.zh: 所以有些听众可能隐约听说过布鲁斯·埃克尔。

sentences.en: He wrote Thinking in C++, and he actually made that book freely available.
sentences.zh: 他写了《Thinking in C++》，而且他实际上把那本书免费公开了。

sentences.en: So decades ago, very, very influential approach to making the stuff available, but also quite a deep and thorough book at the time for anybody who was trying to get into C++.
sentences.zh: 几十年前，这是一种非常有影响力的方式，让人们能获取这些资料，而且对于当时任何想入门C++的人来说，那也是一本相当深刻且详尽的书。

sentences.en: And this is on Bruce Eccle's liSt.
sentences.zh: 而这就在布鲁斯·埃克尔的列表上。

sentences.en: And a guy called Richard Bonson-Heifel, he said, I've submitted a talk.
sentences.zh: 有个叫理查德·邦森-海费尔（Richard Monson-Haefel）的人说，我提交了一个演讲。

sentences.en: I think it was 10 things every software architect should know.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是“每个软件架构师都应该知道的10件事”。

sentences.en: I've submitted a talk to a conference.
sentences.zh: 我向一个会议提交了演讲。

sentences.en: Now I've got the title and they've accepted the talk.
sentences.zh: 现在题目有了，他们也接受了我的演讲。

sentences.en: I need 10 things.
sentences.zh: 我需要10件事。

sentences.en: What do you guys think?
sentences.zh: 你们觉得怎么样？

sentences.en: So everybody started chipping in these ideas.
sentences.zh: 于是大家开始贡献这些想法。

sentences.en: And after about 30 suggestions, he said, you know what?
sentences.zh: 在大约30个建议之后，他说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: There might be something here for a book.
sentences.zh: 这里面可能够出一本书了。

sentences.en: And that was the order.
sentences.zh: 这就是最初的构想。

sentences.en: But then he said, OK, how many should we have?
sentences.zh: 但后来他说，好吧，我们应该有多少条呢？

sentences.en: And he said, I think around 100 is about right.
sentences.zh: 他说，我觉得100条左右差不多。

sentences.en: And he says, but 100 is a slightly cheesy number.
sentences.zh: 他说，但100这个数字有点俗气。

sentences.en: And he says, 99 and 101 are numbers that are trying too hard to not be 100.
sentences.zh: 他说，99和101这两个数字，一看就是为了刻意避开100。

sentences.en: They're too obvious, you know, and he said, 97, that's, you know, it doesn't look like it's trying to be 100, but, you know, it's its own thing.
sentences.zh: 它们太刻意了，你知道，他说，97，那个数字，它看起来不像是在刻意凑成100，它有它自己的个性。

sentences.en: And that really is, that really is it.
sentences.zh: 真的就是这样，原因仅此而已。

sentences.en: That is the only reason for it.
sentences.zh: 这就是唯一的理由。

sentences.en: Good for SEO, right?
sentences.zh: 对SEO（搜索引擎优化）很有利，对吧？

sentences.en: If you search for like, like, like, I'm sure there's a bazillion listicles of 99 things programmers should know or 100 things or 101 things, but 97, that's your number.
sentences.zh: 如果你去搜索，我敢肯定有无数篇类似“程序员应该知道的99件事”或100件事或101件事的列表文章，但97，那就是你的专属数字。

sentences.en: For those that care, it's a strong prime, although you'd never use it in cryptography.
sentences.zh: 对于那些在意的人来说，它是一个强素数，尽管你永远不会在密码学中使用它。

sentences.en: But it is a 97, it's a strong prime, but it is, it is distinct, you know, it's, it's
sentences.zh: 但它确实是97，它是一个强素数，而且它很独特，你知道，它是……

sentences.en: SEO friendly.
sentences.zh: 对SEO很友好。

sentences.en: The reason 100 works is he wanted about two pages.
sentences.zh: 100之所以可行，是因为他想要大约两页纸的篇幅。

sentences.en: So 200 page book, that's actually quite nice.
sentences.zh: 所以200页的书，其实挺不错的。

sentences.en: It doesn't give you depth on each item, but one of the things I really liked about it and why I ended up really pushing this, the program book was, I thought, this is really
sentences.zh: 它不会让你对每一项都有深入了解，但我真正喜欢它的一点，也是我最终极力推崇它的原因，我觉得这本书非常……

sentences.en: useful because it's helpful to start conversations.
sentences.zh: 有用，因为它有助于开启对话。

sentences.en: It's, it's starting point.
sentences.zh: 它是一个起点。

sentences.en: You read something, you can read it in, you know, you can read it in a break.
sentences.zh: 你读到一些东西，你可以在休息的时候读它。

sentences.en: You can look at it and go, hmm, I want to know more, or this has already influenced the way I'm thinking.
sentences.zh: 你可以看一眼，然后心想，嗯，我想了解更多，或者这已经影响了我的思考方式。

sentences.en: Oh, I see what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白他们想表达什么了。

sentences.en: And it's just enough to get you going.
sentences.zh: 而且它足以让你开始行动。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's enough to just change the way that you approach the problem or to present something new to that you perhaps hadn't considered before, but it's not a whole, you
sentences.zh: 有时它足以改变你处理问题的方式，或者为你呈现一些你之前可能没考虑过的新东西，但它不是一个整体，你……

sentences.en: know, you're not committing, you know, an hour or a day of your time to it, but it gives you just enough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不需要投入一小时或一天的时间，但它给你的内容恰到好处。

sentences.en: But it's also quite good for book bombing.
sentences.zh: 而且它也非常适合用来“书本轰炸”。

sentences.en: And I know a couple of people who did that.
sentences.zh: 我知道有几个人就是这么做的。

sentences.en: It's just like, send this to a friend, send it to a friend and make sure you put a post-it on the page that you wanted them to see, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像是，把这个发给朋友，发给朋友，并确保在你希望他们看到的那一页贴上便利贴，你懂吗？

sentences.en: So the physical form of book bombing is quite, they're quite useful.
sentences.zh: 所以这种物理形式的“书本轰炸”非常有用。

sentences.en: A subtle hint.
sentences.zh: 一种微妙的暗示。

sentences.en: Sometimes when you have a disagreement with a colleague about a particular practice, yeah, just leave that book on their, on their, on their table with a little post-it there.
sentences.zh: 有时当你和同事在某种特定做法上有分歧时，是的，就把那本书放在他们的桌子上，贴个小便利贴。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I'm not, you know, the weaponization of 97 things has been interesting, but, but yeah,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我并不是说……97件事的武器化很有趣，但，但确实……

sentences.en: that, so that, that, that was the, that's the rationale for a lot of these things.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中很多事情的逻辑所在。

sentences.en: So, so you, I mean, I, I'm very impressed here because I always like to work smart and not hard.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的很佩服你，因为我总是喜欢聪明地工作，而不是辛苦地工作。

sentences.en: And you've been able to write a book without having to write 97 things yourself by being a curator of things.
sentences.zh: 你能够通过担任策展人的角色，不用自己写97件事就能写出一本书。

sentences.en: And that is, that is, that is very, very commendable.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常值得称赞。

sentences.en: That's, that's, I think, I think there is a, there is an interesting thing because I actually really enjoyed the whole process of doing the editing because it allowed, but
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有一件很有趣的事情，因为我实际上非常享受整个编辑过程，因为它允许……但……

sentences.en: actually the other motivation and why I was happy to do, it was really into doing another book.
sentences.zh: 其实另一个动力，以及为什么我很高兴去做这件事，是因为我真的很想再写一本书。

sentences.en: So I actually really enjoyed it was when you read across what other people do, although sometimes you say, yeah, I know that.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很享受阅读别人所做的事情，尽管有时你会说，是的，我知道那个。

sentences.en: I don't know it the way you know it.
sentences.zh: 但我并不像你那样了解它。

sentences.en: I don't know the way that person knows it.
sentences.zh: 我不了解那个人所知道的方式。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't have written it like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我不会那样写。

sentences.en: And the way they've written it is fresh.
sentences.zh: 他们写的方式很新颖。

sentences.en: If you read across the 97 things and Connor has, you look at some of them and they're real geMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你通读这97件事，康纳（Connor）也读过，你会发现其中一些真的是瑰宝。

sentences.en: And the point is they're not, I, the variety of style and the differences of approaches you go, oh, okay, that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 重点是它们并不……我，那种风格的多样性和方法的差异让你觉得，哦，好吧，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You're not going to get bored.
sentences.zh: 你不会感到无聊。

sentences.en: A single author has control over the narrative.
sentences.zh: 单一作者可以控制叙事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: There's value in that.
sentences.zh: 那是有价值的。

sentences.en: You want that consistency.
sentences.zh: 你想要那种一致性。

sentences.en: But when you're trying to take on, you know, something as complex software development, you probably want to do this by sampling.
sentences.zh: 但当你试图处理像软件开发这样复杂的事情时，你可能想通过抽样来完成。

sentences.en: You know, I want different points of view.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想要不同的观点。

sentences.en: I want to be surprised by stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想要被一些东西惊喜到。

sentences.en: And I was surprised by both books.
sentences.zh: 而这两本书都让我感到惊喜。

sentences.en: And in fact, by some of the other books where I'm looking at it going like, I kind of knew that, but I didn't know it the way they do it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，通过其他一些书，我看着它们心想，我大概知道那个，但我不知道他们那种做法。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't have said it that way, but I like the way they say it.
sentences.zh: 我不会那样说，但我喜欢他们表达的方式。

sentences.en: That's fresh.
sentences.zh: 那很新鲜。

sentences.en: It makes me think of different things.
sentences.zh: 它让我想到了不同的事情。

sentences.en: And that I think is quite valuable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常有价值。

sentences.en: But yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 但确实，你是对的。

sentences.en: Ultimately.
sentences.zh: 归根结底。

sentences.en: How much did you have to edit to get to like a consistent language or to get to consistent like, like, is it, is it very lightly edited or is it more like you had to draft things a
sentences.zh: 为了达到一致的语言或一致的风格，你必须进行多少编辑，或者说，它是经过轻微编辑的，还是说你必须起草……

sentences.en: little bit and reshape things a bit?
sentences.zh: 一点点，并对内容进行了一些重塑？

sentences.en: I, uh, it, it, it depended, it depended on the, it depended on the contribution.
sentences.zh: 我，呃，这取决于，这取决于贡献的内容。

sentences.en: I mean, sometimes, and actually that was another thing I explicitly, although I don't know if this was Richard Monsenhaifel's original intention, but I explicitly made a point when
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时，实际上这也是我明确提出的另一件事，虽然我不知道这是否是理查德·蒙森-海费尔最初的意图，但我明确表示……

sentences.en: I was, um, you know, uh, when people would contact me, I'd, I'd sort of talk about this at conferences and say, you know, let me know if you're interested in contributing.
sentences.zh: 当人们联系我时，我会在会议上谈论这件事，并说，如果你有兴趣投稿，请告诉我。

sentences.en: I mean, I contacted a few people saying, Hey, would you be interested in contributing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我联系了一些人说，嘿，你有兴趣投稿吗？

sentences.en: But actually a lot actually came, uh, from people I don't know, um, uh, just because I advertised it on Twitter at the time and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上很多内容来自我不认识的人，只是因为我当时在Twitter上做了宣传之类的。

sentences.en: And I made a real point about saying on the landing page, it was done through a wiki.
sentences.zh: 我在着陆页上明确指出，这是通过维基完成的。

sentences.en: I made a point on the landing page.
sentences.zh: 我在着陆页上强调了这一点。

sentences.en: It's just like, if you're not comfortable with writing, perhaps English isn't your first language.
sentences.zh: 就像是，如果你不擅长写作，也许英语不是你的母语。

sentences.en: Don't worry.
sentences.zh: 别担心。

sentences.en: It's, you're talking about 500 pages.
sentences.zh: 你说的是500页的内容。

sentences.en: I can, I can do the editing.
sentences.zh: 我可以，我可以负责编辑。

sentences.en: If you're, if you're worried about language, I can, I want your enthusiasm and your knowledge.
sentences.zh: 如果你担心语言问题，我可以，我想要的是你的热情和知识。

sentences.en: Give me the story and I can shape it.
sentences.zh: 把故事给我，我可以塑造它。

sentences.en: You know, so sometimes I'm getting stuff and I'm having to do a lot of syntactic level work or phrasing and voice stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我收到内容，必须在句法层面或措辞和语气上做大量工作。

sentences.en: Um, and I always did that one-to-one via email, obviously, but one-to-one with the author.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我显然总是通过电子邮件一对一地进行，与作者一对一沟通。

sentences.en: And I put a lot of effort in.
sentences.zh: 我投入了大量精力。

sentences.en: So I would say there was a lot of effort involved in the writing because I want, I wanted to have a proper consent and agreement and to give, you know, just say, is this okay with
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说写作过程中投入了大量精力，因为我想要获得适当的同意和认可，并且只是说，这对你来说可以吗？

sentences.en: you?
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: But whereas for other people, uh, there's a couple in there.
sentences.zh: 但对于其他人，呃，里面有几篇。

sentences.en: I didn't even move a comma.
sentences.zh: 我连一个逗号都没动。

sentences.en: It's just like, it's just like, I don't want to touch this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我不想碰这个。

sentences.en: This is so good as it is.
sentences.zh: 它本身就已经很棒了。

sentences.en: Or actually that captures their voice perfectly.
sentences.zh: 或者实际上那完美地捕捉到了他们的声音。

sentences.en: Um, so it varied, but overall the whole set is I edited all the items before I selected.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以情况各不相同，但总的来说，我在选择之前编辑了所有的条目。

sentences.en: So I had nearly 200 items as they came in.
sentences.zh: 所以我收到了近200个条目。

sentences.en: And so I'd be doing something.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在做一些事情。

sentences.en: How many submissions you got?
sentences.zh: 你收到了多少投稿？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's 170 submissions around 170.
sentences.zh: 是的，大约170份投稿，170左右。

sentences.en: And so I was editing everything pretty much as it came in.
sentences.zh: 所以我几乎在收到每一份投稿时都在进行编辑。

sentences.en: I created a proper workflow for myself.
sentences.zh: 我为自己创建了一个合适的工作流程。

sentences.en: Um, and so there was a continuous amount, you know, in a given week or on a given day, I would always be devoting a certain amount of time to it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以有一个持续的工作量，你知道，在某一周或某一天，我总是会投入一定的时间。

sentences.en: And, um, so there was certainly a, uh, an effort there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这肯定是一份努力。

sentences.en: Um, but I found that, but ultimately I found that easier, um, than, than writing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我发现，最终我发现这比写作更容易。

sentences.en: I mean, I've written a couple of books myself and it's just like, I don't know, uh, it's, uh, it works differently for different people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我自己写过几本书，感觉就像，我不知道，这对不同的人来说效果不同。

sentences.en: But, um, all I will say is that my wife told me after, um, after, uh, 97 things, she said,
sentences.zh: 但是，我只想说，我妻子在《97件事》之后告诉我，她说，

sentences.en: Kevlin, you're a lot more pleasant when you're editing a book than when you're writing one.
sentences.zh: 凯夫林（Kevlin），你在编辑书的时候比你在写书的时候要讨人喜欢得多。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, as a human being to live with, I, you know, okay, I'll get that, you know?
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道，作为一个一起生活的人，我，你知道，好吧，我明白了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, uh, I can see that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以是的，我能理解。

sentences.en: It's funny because despite my, despite my, my joke earlier, um, I actually can imagine that,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为尽管我之前开了个玩笑，但我确实能想象到，

sentences.en: uh, uh, having to be an editor for 97 different, was it 97 unique individuals that submitted?
sentences.zh: 呃，要成为97个不同的人的编辑，是97个独立投稿的人吗？

sentences.en: No, 73 unique individuals.
sentences.zh: 不，是73个独立的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Having to be, having to, to, uh, interact with and work with 73 different people, some of whom you had to go back and forth with, uh, edits on and you had to make sure
sentences.zh: 要与73个不同的人互动和工作，其中一些人你必须来回沟通编辑，而且你必须确保……

sentences.en: you got everybody's, you know, sign off and most of whom I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你得到了每个人的认可，而且他们中的大多数我都不认识。

sentences.en: So that's the other thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一回事。

sentences.en: This is actually, this actually sounds like a good, a good bit of work, a different type of work.
sentences.zh: 这听起来确实是一项不错的工作，一种不同类型的工作。

sentences.en: Um, I guess that maybe the nice thing about, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这也许是……的好处，

sentences.en: uh, this versus writing a book on your own is if you're writing a book on your own, you, uh, have to push the work out.
sentences.zh: 呃，这与自己写书相比，如果你自己写书，你必须推动工作进展。

sentences.en: Whereas, uh, if you're an editor in this, this sense, you have all this stuff coming in, you have to keep up with it, but you don't, you don't end up in that, like that, you know,
sentences.zh: 而如果你是这种意义上的编辑，你会有所有这些东西涌进来，你必须跟上进度，但你不会陷入那种，你知道，

sentences.en: that writer's block mode.
sentences.zh: 那种“写作障碍”模式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I, I, I mean, particularly, I guess I'm listed as the editor.
sentences.zh: 我，我的意思是，特别是，我想我被列为编辑。

sentences.en: I would call myself the, the project driver.
sentences.zh: 我会称自己为项目驱动者。

sentences.en: Cause it was kind of like, I really kind of pushed this one.
sentences.zh: 因为这有点像，我确实推动了这个项目。

sentences.en: Cause I've noticed that a couple of the other editors in the series, they're very, very passive.
sentences.zh: 因为我注意到系列中的其他几位编辑，他们非常、非常被动。

sentences.en: In other words, they say I'm going to be the editor and then they expect the publisher to go out and do this.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们说我要当编辑，然后他们期望出版商出去做这些事。

sentences.en: And I said, no, no, no, this is my baby.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，不，不，这是我的心血结晶。

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to, I want, you know, this is going to be social media, the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我要，我想要，这将会是社交媒体，整个事情。

sentences.en: I'm interested.
sentences.zh: 我很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm genuinely interested in what people have to offer here.
sentences.zh: 我真心对人们在这里提供的贡献感兴趣。

sentences.en: So I'm going to drive this project.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算推动这个项目。

sentences.en: And it is, you know, as you say, it's, it's got a different enjoyment, but it's got a steady state to it.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，它有不同的乐趣，但它有一个稳定的状态。

sentences.en: And that's what I appreciated.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所欣赏的。

sentences.en: Um, but I think there's also an irony after I finished, I coauthored two pattern, uh, two pattern books with, um, uh, Frank Bushman and Doug Schmidt and, uh, Frank Bushman made
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为在我完成后还有一个讽刺之处，我与弗兰克·布什曼（Frank Buschmann）和道格·施密特（Doug Schmidt）合著了两本模式书，呃，弗兰克·布什曼指出，我突然意识到我所做的一切都是在为别人的书做贡献，或者，你知道，过去做过类似的事情，或者合著。
